chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: Receiving notice from Moe Gale
summary: While Duke is away, the band is reorganized and Moe Gale gives Thomas two weeks' notice, which Mills overturns.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So the Cotton Club, you guys... Now, Duke left to do...
"Check and Double Check" is what he did there.
And Mills... Now, here's another funny thing. I got fired! I had my two-week notice.

Well, they just wanted to get... They thought they was getting a... Gale and them was gettin' a guy they thought was better than me. So it didn't bother me too much, because I always was able to get a job around New York. I didn't worry. But I went down... The next day... the next week I had to go downtown with Cab to check over some songs. I told him, I said, "I got my notice" He said, "What?! You got your notice. They got to be crazy." See, I guess I influenced Mills, because I made this arrangement
Who gave you your notice? Cab?
The Savoy. See, Moe Gale was the first manager of the band. But the gangs...
That's the Savoy. They didn't have anything to do with the Cotton Club.
But he had us before we went to the Cotton Club. So Moe Gale was the one that gave me the notice. So I went to tell...
Cab didn't have nothin' to say about it, huh.

No. Because Cab had just gotten the band himself. He didn't have nothin' to say about it. At least he didn't say nothin' about it. So when I went to... Mills was the head guy, because he was the one getting us all these jobs.
